concepts.def: Warming melts ice -> less reflection -> more warming

walkthroughs.body_html:
Ice cores, tree rings and CO2 records show a sharp rise in CO2 since 1850.

Temperature has risen about 1.1 degrees C in the same period.

The IPCC reviews thousands of studies and is very confident humans are the main cause.

Media often simplify or sensationalise.

Some claims are not peer-reviewed - check the source.

Models are predictions; uncertainty does not mean no risk.

Switch to renewables (wind, solar).

Improve energy efficiency; insulate homes; carbon capture and storage.

Each has costs and limits - policy and consumer choice both matter.

mcqs.q: Which is mitigation rather than adaptation?
Carbon footprint of a product means:
options: total greenhouse gases over its life cycle

mcqs.q: How does a catalyst speed up a reaction?
options: It provides an alternative reaction pathway with a lower activation energy.
A catalyst gives extra kinetic energy to the reactant particles.
The forward reaction stops once the reverse reaction begins.
A catalyst lowers the activation energy of the original reaction pathway.

mcqs.q: At dynamic equilibrium, what is happening to the reactions?
options: Forward and reverse reactions continue at equal rates; concentrations remain constant.
A catalyst gives extra kinetic energy to the reactant particles.
The forward reaction stops once the reverse reaction begins.
Both reactions stop because the system has reached balance.

mcqs.q: When an acid neutralises an alkali, what is the pH of the resulting solution?
options: A catalyst gives extra kinetic energy to the reactant particles.
Neutralisation always produces a solution with pH exactly 7 regardless of the acid and base used.
Approximately 7 if equivalent amounts of strong acid and strong alkali react — but it varies with strength.
Neutralisation always produces a solution with pH 0.
